demo.lead: Four pieces of the Material theme, running in your browser with sample data. Nothing is sent anywhere.
demo.motionNote: Animations follow the Motion setting in the display settings menu at the top of the page. Calm and Off skip the confetti, as the theme does.
demo.signinB: Select Sign in with a passkey to watch the device prompt and the welcome message. Sign in with an empty password to see the error shake.
demo.signinText: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or security key, or with your username and password.
demo.paletteB: Sample courses, activities and settings from a Moodle site. Add blocks to build a pattern: try Starts with, then type Intro. Type ( alone to see the invalid state.
demo.celebrateB: What the deployer shows when a site goes live. Moodle success messages get the same confetti.
demo.liveB: Moodle is installed on your server, the Material theme is active and the secure tunnel is connected.
demo.errorB: When something fails, the screen shakes once, explains what happened and offers the next step.
demo.errText: Everything before this step is kept. Your server still runs Moodle on port 8080; only the public link is missing.
demo.fix1: Run the guided login again so the tunnel certificate is refreshed.
demo.fix2: Or switch to a quick tunnel, which needs no account.
page.demo.title: Demo
deploy.lead: Run the Docker stack on any machine, put it online with a Cloudflare tunnel, or let the desktop deployer do it over SSH.
deploy.oneCmd: One command installs and starts everything. Run it on the server as a user who can use Docker or sudo.
deploy.s1b: A terminal menu asks for the site name, administrator and how people reach the site. Press Enter to accept each suggestion.
deploy.s2b: The installer generates the database and administrator passwords and writes the .env file. Docker is installed first if it is missing, after you agree.
deploy.s3b: The first start installs Moodle and applies the Material defaults. The installer waits until the site answers.
deploy.s4b: The installer prints the address and the administrator sign-in. The setup wizard opens when you first sign in.
deploy.reconfB: Run the same command again to restart with your saved answers, or add --reconfigure to change them.
deploy.autoB: Add --yes to skip the menu and set the answers with MM_ variables. Anything you leave out uses the suggestion, and passwords are still generated.
deploy.manualB: Prefer to do it by hand? The installer also works from a clone of the repository, using its Compose file.
deploy.quickB: No account. You get a random address that changes when the tunnel restarts. Choose it in the installer menu.
deploy.namedB: A permanent address on a domain in your Cloudflare account. Paste a tunnel token from the dashboard into the installer.
deploy.tunnelManual: The installer sets these up for you. To switch an existing stack by hand, from the stack folder:
deploy.envB: The installer writes these to .env for you. They are listed here for reference.
deploy.updateB: Back up both volumes, then pull the new image from the stack folder. Moodle's upgrade runs when the container starts.
deploy.appB: Material Moodle Deployer will deploy the stack to any Linux server you can reach over SSH, install Docker if it is missing, and set up a Cloudflare tunnel with a guided sign-in. It is still being built, so there is no installer yet.
page.deploy.title: Deploy
docs.lead: One article per feature. Each covers what it does, its settings, what can go wrong, security and privacy, and how to verify it.
docs.installB: On a Linux server with or without Docker, one command installs everything and prints your link. See Deploy for the options.
docs.whereB: Upstream Moodle files stay as they are. Everything Material Moodle adds sits in a small overlay, so merging new Moodle releases stays simple.
docs.buildB: The plugins' browser modules are written by hand in amd/src. Moodle loads amd/build, so rebuild after every change. The script does not need Moodle's Grunt toolchain.
page.docs.title: Docs
dl.lead: Every release is published on GitHub with its files and notes.
dl.stackB: material-moodle-stack-<version>.zip with the Compose file and .env.example.
dl.pluginsB: The theme, passkey and Material tools plugins as zips for an existing Moodle 6 site.
dl.deployerB: Installers for Windows, macOS and Linux will be attached once the app is finished. They are not code signed, so your system may warn before opening them.
dl.tags: Release tags look like material-v1.0.0-42: the version, then the build number, so every build has a unique tag. Each release also has a dim sum code name.
dl.existing: Install the plugins on an existing site
dl.existingB: The plugins require Moodle 6. Unzip each package into its folder, then visit Site administration to finish the upgrade.
page.download.title: Download
features.lead: Material Moodle adds three plugins, a Docker stack and a desktop deployer to Moodle 6. Each card opens a detailed article.
feat.themeB: One seed colour builds the full light and dark palette, with rounded shapes, density and motion levels.
feat.motionB: Expressive, calm or off. Devices that ask for reduced motion always get the calm version.
feat.paletteB: Ctrl+Shift+F searches courses, page links and settings. Pattern blocks build a regular expression for you.
feat.searchboxesB: Filter boxes across Moodle get the same Regex and Ignore case switches and the same blocks.
feat.ctxB: A Material menu with shortcuts for links, images, code, selected text and the page itself.
feat.copyB: Every code block gets a Copy button that confirms when the text is on the clipboard.
feat.celebrateB: Success messages burst with confetti; errors shake and flash so they are not missed.
feat.signinB: Your own heading, text, labels and optional photo beside a large passkey button.
feat.passkeyB: Sign in with a fingerprint, face, screen lock or security key. Passwords keep working.
feat.managerB: Each person adds, renames and removes their own passkeys from their preferences.
feat.studentB: Creates the account and a Discord message with the username and password in separate code blocks.
feat.first: Forced password change and optional passkey
feat.firstB: New students choose their own password, then may add a passkey. The passkey step can be skipped.
feat.vocabB: Upload a JSON file of replacement words, shown only to the students and cohorts you choose.
feat.wordingB: Rename Teacher, Student and Assignment across the whole site from one page.
feat.labels: Activity type names and personal titles
feat.labelsB: Show one assignment as a "Dropbox", add Post a new Dropbox buttons, and give people titles that keep their role.
feat.wizardB: Colour, sign-in page, passkeys, vocabulary and wording in six guided steps, with Back, Next, Skip and resume.
feat.dockerB: PostgreSQL, Moodle and cron containers that install Moodle and apply the Material defaults on first start.
feat.deployerB: One click deploys the stack to any Linux server you can reach over SSH.
feat.tunnelB: A free quick link with no account, or a named tunnel on your own domain.

home.lead: A full theme, passkey sign-in, and a one-click deployer that installs everything on your server and puts it online.
home.f1b: Seed colour palettes, dark mode, rounded shapes and motion across every Moodle page.
home.f2b: Fingerprint, face or security key. Students can add one after their first sign-in.
home.f3b: A desktop app installs Docker, Moodle and the theme on any SSH server.
home.f4b: A quick link with no account, or your own domain with a guided sign-in.
home.f5b: Ctrl+Shift+F searches courses, pages and settings, with a visual pattern builder.
home.f6b: New accounts come with a ready-to-paste message for Discord and a forced password change.
home.runningLead: Real screenshots from a Material Moodle site, on a laptop and on a phone.
home.termLead: One command on any Linux server. A menu asks a few questions, generates the passwords and settings, starts Moodle and prints your link.
home.demoLead: The demo runs the sign-in page, the command palette with its regex builder, a celebration and an error screen, all without a server.
page.home.title: Home
pk.lead: Sign in once with your face, fingerprint or security key. No password to remember, and nothing to phish.
pk.w1b: A passkey only works on the site it was made for, so a fake sign-in page gets nothing.
pk.w2b: The device offers the passkey. Students do not type a username or a password.
pk.w3b: Passkeys are added to existing accounts. The password stays as a fallback.
pk.on1b: Site administration › Plugins › Authentication › Manage authentication › Passkeys. The Docker first run does this for you.
pk.on2b: Passkeys belong to one host name. Use your own domain or a named tunnel before people add them.
pk.on3b: From Preferences › Passkeys, or from the optional step after a new account's first sign-in.
pk.managerB: Everyone manages their own passkeys: add one with a name such as "My phone", see when each was last used, rename or remove it. Keep at least two passkeys on different devices.
pk.shot: The passkey manager in a running site. Passkey sign-in is verified end to end in the browser checks.
pk.more1: How a sign-in works, settings and security.
pk.more3: The three-step first sign-in for new students.
pk.more4: A working copy of the passkey button in the demo.
page.passkeys.title: Passkeys
st.lead: Add a student in one form and paste their sign-in details straight into Discord. Username and password each sit in their own code block, so one tap copies each.
st.f1b: The username is made from the name if you leave it empty. Email is optional.
st.f2b: A temporary password is generated, for example two words and a number.
st.f3b: One button copies the whole message. Send it as a direct message.
st.f4b: The student must choose a new password, then may add a passkey.
st.pasteB: This is the default message for a student called Alex Student. Try the copy buttons: the whole message, the username alone, or the password alone.
st.secret: Treat the message as a secret. The password is shown only once and the student must change it.
st.more: Read the Add a student article
page.students.title: Students
vo.lead: Use the words your school uses. Three tools, from the whole site down to one activity.
vo.t1: For everyone: rename Teacher, Student and Assignment on every page.
vo.t2: For chosen people: a JSON file of replacement words, shown only after sign-in.
vo.t3: For one activity or person: show an assignment as a "Dropbox", or call one teacher "Coach".
vo.formatB: A pack is a UTF-8 JSON object with schemaVersion 1 and an entries object of original words and replacements.
vo.strict: Any failed rule rejects the whole file with a specific message, and the previous pack stays in place.
vo.u1: Choose a file on Site administration › Users › Material tools › Custom vocabulary, or drop a .json file anywhere on the site as a manager.
vo.u2: Pick who sees it: nobody, everyone signed in, or selected students and cohorts (the default).
vo.u3: Tick Custom vocabulary on Add a student to choose a new student straight away.
vo.u4: Signed-out pages, guests and people outside the audience always see the original wording.
